title: Simply perfect: every possible excellence — God alone
source_text: IV. Simpliciter vero perfectum est id cui nihil omnino deest, & quod habet omnem excellentiam possibilem. Talis perfectio nulli creaturae competit, sed est proprium naturae divinae attributum. Omnis enim creatura perfectionem habet certam & determinatam, haec illam, ista aliam: sed Deus in se continet quicquid haberi potest perfectionis, nec cogitari potest ulla excellentia cujus natura divina sit expers.
pass_a_gloss: But simply perfect is that to which nothing at all is lacking, and which has every possible excellence. Such perfection befits no creature, but is a proper attribute of the divine nature. For every creature has a certain and determinate perfection, this one that, that one another: but God contains in Himself whatever of perfection can be had, nor can any excellence be thought of of which the divine nature is devoid.
pass_b_english: Simply perfect: nothing lacking; every possible excellence.
No creature — only the divine nature.
Creatures have bounded perfections; God holds them all.

lemmas.gloss: a proper attribute of the divine nature

rejected: some creature can be simply perfect
